# Campaign: 13 chapters of standard enemies, balanced to the economy

*Generated by `Tools/gen_campaign_data.py` from `Tests/campaign_model.h`. Do not edit by hand. Every number is a **PLACEHOLDER**
(MAIN leaves enemy stats, level counts per chapter, rewards and rates OPEN or DEFERRED); the owner replaces them.*

Owner request, 2026-10-05: fill chapters 2-13 with levels made of standard balancing enemies, a mini boss at the end of every
level (in a chapter's last level, the mini boss in the section before the boss), and balance each stage to the currency,
levels and operators a player has at that point, a bit harder so that some grinding is needed.

## What was built

Owner rebalance, 2026-10-06: a much heavier health and damage increase per operator level (+6% per level, was +1%) with the
enemies scaled to match (Chapter 1 included); stage rewards start at 800 Gold, 250 Bytes and 2 Angel hearts per clear and 50 Diamonds on the
first clear; a new account starts with 300 Diamonds and nothing else; tickets come from the story quests.

- **13 chapters x 8 levels** (Chapter 1 keeps its original eight level layouts; the other twelve follow it, PLACEHOLDER). Levels unlock in order,
  chapters unlock when the previous chapter's boss is cleared; the admin account has every level open.
- **Every level** has 2-5 sections of 10-30 enemies (MAIN section 7) and ends with **one mini boss**. A **chapter's last level** has
  five sections: the mini boss closes section 4, the **chapter boss** closes section 5 (so the mini boss is the stage before the boss).
- **Seven enemy archetypes**: basic (melee), ranged, mage (area blasts), brute (tank), assassin (high damage, close range, low
  health), mini boss, boss. They appear chapter by chapter: ranged in 2, mages in 3, assassins in 4; from chapter 5 every chapter leans
  on one or two of them (a PLACEHOLDER mix, no lore).
- **Balance**: a reference player (below) fixes how many levels, upgrade stars and operators a player has at each stage; the enemy
  health and damage scale from there and each stage is made a bit harder than that player's pace, so about one replay of an earlier
  stage is needed per level and two or three before a boss.

## Enemy archetypes (base numbers, multiplied by the stage's scales)

| Archetype | Health | Damage | Every | Telegraph | Speed | Reach | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Angel | 2000 | 40 | 1.6 s | 0.5 s | 330 | melee | Basic melee enemy: walks up and hits. |
| Ranged angel | 1400 | 32 | 2.0 s | 0.6 s | 300 | 1500 cm | Ranged enemy: keeps its distance and shoots after a short telegraph. |
| Mage angel | 1600 | 95 | 4.0 s | 1.5 s | 280 | 1300 cm | Mage enemy: marks the ground under the operator and blasts it (area damage); move out of the circle. Blast radius 380 cm. |
| Heavy angel | 5000 | 80 | 1.6 s | 0.5 s | 260 | melee | Brute enemy: a slow tank with a hard hit. |
| Assassin angel | 900 | 75 | 1.0 s | 0.3 s | 560 | melee | Assassin enemy: dashes in and strikes fast and hard; very low health. |
| MINI-BOSS | 40000 | 120 | 1.6 s | 0.5 s | 300 | melee | Sub boss: the end of every level. |
| CHAPTER BOSS | 120000 | 200 | 1.6 s | 0.5 s | 280 | melee | Main boss: the end of every chapter; adds a telegraphed slam. Slam 300 every 7 s, radius 700 cm. |

## The reference player

A player who clears the stages in order, spends everything on a team of three operators (all at the same level), and replays the newest
stage when the next one asks for more levels than they have. Assumptions, all PLACEHOLDER:

- Income: `StageReward` (BIBCampaign.h), paid on every clear: Gold 800, Bytes 250 and Angel hearts 2 at stage 1, Gold and Bytes growing by 12%
  of that per stage, hearts by 6%
  per stage (stage 103: Gold 10590, Bytes 3310, hearts 14); a boss level pays x2. Diamonds on the first clear only: 50 in Chapter 1, +10 per chapter,
  x3 on a boss level. Story quests (BIBMetaOps.h) add 20-50 Diamonds after level 3, Gold and Bytes or Angel hearts after level 6, and the
  chapter's Regular tickets (10 for Chapter 1, 1 after that) at its end. Daily and weekly quests are left out of the model (bonus income).
- Costs: the real rules (`LevelUpCost`, `HeartGateCost`, level cap 100 + 20 per upgrade star); 85% of the currency reaches the three
  team operators (the rest goes to equipment and other operators).
- Operators: every pull (Diamonds / 300, plus the story-quest tickets) can duplicate a team member; duplicates give upgrade stars (5% damage
  and defence each); equipment adds up to 20%; a bigger roster adds up to 10% (better team choice). Expected summons by the last stage: 103.
- "A bit harder": a stage asks for the team level the player would have after 5.0 more clears of the newest stage (12.0 before a chapter boss,
  chapter 2 eases in from 30% of that). That is the grind.
- Result: the reference player needs **455 replays over the 104 stages** (5.4 clears per stage), and reaches team level 140 at the last stage
  with 2 upgrade stars. The base level cap is 100 and each upgrade star (a duplicate summon) adds 20, so the last chapters need duplicates of
  the team's operators; a player without them can only make up the gap with skill.
- Fights: the operators' damage, the enemies' danger order, crowd damage, uptime and dodging are assumptions of the fluid model in
  `Tests/campaign_model.h` (reference team Luna, Plack, Kuu). The **threat** column below is the model's relative difficulty of a level,
  Chapter 1 level 7 = 1.00; the section sizes of the generated levels were solved to hit the **target**. Nothing here was play-tested: the
  owner's first play-through will say how the real fights compare.

## Chapter 11 - Return to Nowhere (a walk, no enemies)

Return to Nowhere (owner level idea, final): no levels, no bosses, no enemies, no rewards - one walk of about five
minutes through `L_Ch11_ReturnToNowhere`; walking out clears the chapter (stage ids 81-88). Nothing to grind; the team
arrives at Chapter 12 at about level 121.

## Regenerating

`python3 Tools/gen_campaign_data.py` rebuilds `BIBRules/BIBCampaignData.inc` and this file. Change the reference player's
assumptions in `Tests/campaign_model.h`, the rewards and archetypes in `BIBRules/BIBCampaign.*`, then rerun it and
`Tests/run_core_tests.sh`.
